claims.text: A thin niobium interlayer between HEA layers will create controlled interface coherency.
The Nb-induced interface coherency will enable a tunable transition from diffusion-mediated creep to dislocation-mediated creep at elevated temperature.
The proposed Nb interlayer thickness is approximately 5 nm.
The Nb interlayer will be deposited by magnetron sputtering between consecutive HEA layers.
The proposed post-annealing treatment is 700°C for 50 hours.
Both diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated mechanisms are active under the proposed elevated-temperature creep conditions.
The Nb interlayer modifies the coherency of interfaces between HEA layers.
The Nb interlayer creates an intermediate zone with partially matched lattice parameters.
The Nb-containing intermediate zone has enhanced atomic mobility.
Nb has atomic mobility intermediate between the relevant HEA layers or constituents.
Nb partially lattice-matches the HEA layers.
At lower stresses or shorter times, enhanced interface diffusivity caused by the Nb interlayer promotes diffusion-mediated creep.
At higher stresses or longer times, the Nb-modified interface supports dislocation motion.
The Nb interlayer shifts the dominant creep mechanism as stress or elapsed time changes.
HEA multilayers containing the Nb interlayer will exhibit a clear shift in the creep-mechanism transition point relative to multilayers without the interlayer.
HEA multilayers containing the Nb interlayer will have improved overall creep performance relative to the control.
The proposed effect is expected near 700°C and for an Nb interlayer thickness around 5 nm.
Changing interlayer thickness, annealing time, or annealing temperature may alter the creep-mechanism transition.
The exact stress or temperature thresholds for mechanism switching depend on microstructure and grain-boundary characteristics.
